statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum of the set of all k with 0 <= k <= len(costs) for which there exists a set S of exactly k distinct indices, each satisfying 0 <= i < len(costs), such that the sum of costs[i] over i in S is at most coins. In other words, r is the largest number of bars the boy can buy, where buying a bar costs its price, each bar is bought at most once, and the total spent may not exceed coins.
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r (it never fails, in particular it does not overflow or index out of bounds), and 0 <= r <= len(costs).
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exist r distinct indices i_1, ..., i_r, each satisfying 0 <= i_j < len(costs), such that costs[i_1] + ... + costs[i_r] <= coins. (For r = 0 the family is empty and the sum is 0.)
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and for every set S of r + 1 distinct indices with 0 <= i < len(costs) for each i in S, the sum of costs[i] over i in S is strictly greater than coins. (When r = len(costs) no such set S exists and the condition holds vacuously.)
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and if s_0 <= s_1 <= ... <= s_{len(costs)-1} is the multiset of values costs[0], ..., costs[len(costs)-1] arranged in non-decreasing order, then s_0 + s_1 + ... + s_{r-1} <= coins (the empty sum when r = 0 is 0).
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and if s_0 <= s_1 <= ... <= s_{len(costs)-1} is the multiset of values costs[0], ..., costs[len(costs)-1] in non-decreasing order and r < len(costs), then s_0 + s_1 + ... + s_r > coins.
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r <= coins.
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r <= the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(costs) and costs[i] <= coins.
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if costs[i] > coins for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs).
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(costs) if and only if costs[0] + costs[1] + ... + costs[len(costs)-1] <= coins.
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and for every k with 0 <= k <= r there exists a set S of exactly k distinct indices, each satisfying 0 <= i < len(costs), such that the sum of costs[i] over i in S is at most coins.
preconditions: 1 <= len(costs); for every i with 0 <= i < len(costs), 1 <= costs[i] <= 100000; 1 <= coins <= 100000000.
